summary: A place for one store on the B-52H: six on each of its two under-wing pylons, eight on the rotary launcher in its bomb bay

stations.name: left pylon, forward lower
stations.note: six stores a pylon, as the article has the cruise missiles ('12 missiles on underwing pylons'): two rows of three in tandem - one under the beam, one on each shoulder. Its place estimated on hangar's design of the B-52H: the pylon 6.0 m out (between the fuselage and the inboard engine pods, judged from the type's layout, not measured), the stores' middle 40 % of the local chord aft of the leading edge, the shoulders 1.3 m and the lower store 1.6 m below the wing's under side; the rows 2.5 m apart (a 500 lb bomb is 2.21 m long). Its limit a 2,000 lb class store's: engineering assumptions

stations.name: bomb bay 1
stations.note: eight stores on the bay's rotary launcher ('another eight missiles on a rotary launcher fitted in the bomb bay'): round its axis, 45 deg apart, each released from its own place (a real launcher turns the next store to the bottom: not modelled). Its place estimated on hangar's design: the launcher's axis on the centreline at the empty CG's station, 0.8 m above the belly; its ring's radius a 500 lb bomb's eight just touching. Its limit a 2,000 lb class store's: engineering assumptions
